ARTICLE X - MISCELLANEOUS
2

This CREDIT AGREEMENT is entered into as of the Closing Date among
Marrowfield Packaging Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Borrower"), each
lender from time to time party hereto (collectively, the "Lenders" and individually, a
"Lender"), and Halden Bay National Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent, Swing Line
Lender, and L/C Issuer.
PRELIMINARY STATEMENTS:
The Borrower has requested that the Lenders provide a term loan facility and a revolving
credit facility, the proceeds of which will be used on the Closing Date to refinance all
indebtedness outstanding under the Existing Credit Agreement, to pay fees and expenses
incurred in connection with this Agreement, and thereafter for working capital, capital
expenditures, Permitted Acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes. The Lenders
are willing to do so on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein. In
consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, the parties hereto
covenant and agree as follows:
ARTICLE I
DEFINITIONS AND ACCOUNTING TERMS
1.01 Defined Terms. As used in this Agreement, the following terms have the
meanings set forth below:
"Acquisition" means the acquisition, whether by purchase, merger, or
otherwise, of all or substantially all of the assets of, or a business line, product line, or
division of, any Person, or of more than fifty percent of the Equity Interests of any
Person.
"Additional Lender" has the meaning specified in Section 2.16(c), being any
bank, financial institution, or other institutional lender that agrees to provide all or part of
an Incremental Facility and is reasonably acceptable to the Administrative Agent.
"Administrative Agent" means Halden Bay National Bank, N.A., in its
capacity as administrative agent under any of the Loan Documents, or any successor
administrative agent appointed under Article IX.
"Agent Parties" means the Administrative Agent and its Related Parties, in
their capacities as such, including in connection with the Platform and the distribution of
Borrower Materials.
4

"Anti-Corruption Laws" means the United States Foreign Corrupt Practices
Act of 1977, the UK Bribery Act 2010, and all other laws, rules, and regulations of any
jurisdiction applicable to the Borrower or its Subsidiaries from time to time concerning or
relating to bribery or corruption.
"Administrative Agent's Office" means the Administrative Agent's address
and, as appropriate, account as set forth on Schedule 10.02, or such other address or
account as the Administrative Agent may from time to time notify to the Borrower and
the Lenders.
"Affiliate" means, with respect to a specified Person, another Person that
directly, or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, Controls or is Controlled by or
is under common Control with the Person specified; provided that no Lender shall be an
Affiliate of the Borrower solely by reason of holding Loans.
"Aggregate Commitments" means the Commitments of all the Lenders,
which on the Closing Date are $350,000,000, consisting of Revolving Credit
Commitments of $100,000,000 and Term A Commitments of $250,000,000.
"Applicable Revolving Credit Percentage" means, with respect to any
Revolving Credit Lender at any time, the percentage of the Revolving Credit Facility
represented by that Lender's Revolving Credit Commitment at that time, subject to
adjustment as provided in Section 2.15; if the Revolving Credit Commitments have
terminated or expired, the Applicable Revolving Credit Percentage of each Lender is
determined based on its most recent Applicable Revolving Credit Percentage, giving
effect to any subsequent assignments.
"Applicable Percentage" means, with respect to any Lender at any time, (a) in
respect of the Revolving Credit Facility, the percentage of the Revolving Credit Facility
represented by that Lender's Revolving Credit Commitment, and (b) in respect of the
Term A Facility, the percentage of the outstanding principal amount of the Term A Loans
held by that Lender, in each case as set forth opposite its name on Schedule 2.01 or in the
Assignment and Assumption by which it becomes a party.
"Applicable Rate" means, from time to time, the following percentages per
annum, based upon the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio as set forth in the most recent
Compliance Certificate received by the Administrative Agent under Section 6.02(a);
provided that from the Closing Date until the first Business Day after delivery of the
Compliance Certificate for the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026, Pricing Level 3
5

applies:
Pricing Level Consolidated Total Leverage Term SOFR Base RateCommitment
Ratio Loans and Loans Fee
Letter of Credit
Fee
1 < 1.50:1.00 1.375% 0.375% 0.175%
2 >= 1.50:1.00 but < 2.25:1.00 1.625% 0.625% 0.200%
3 >= 2.25:1.00 but < 3.00:1.00 1.875% 0.875% 0.250%
4 >= 3.00:1.00 but < 3.50:1.00 2.125% 1.125% 0.300%
5 >= 3.50:1.00 2.375% 1.375% 0.350%
"Approved Fund" means any Fund that is administered or managed by (a) a
Lender, (b) an Affiliate of a Lender, or (c) an entity or an Affiliate of an entity that
administers or manages a Lender.
"Approved Bank" means a commercial bank organized under the laws of the
United States or any State thereof having combined capital and surplus of not less than
$500,000,000 and a long-term unsecured debt rating of at least A or A2.
"Asset Sale" means any Disposition of property by the Borrower or any
Subsidiary (including any sale and leaseback transaction and any issuance of Equity
Interests by a Subsidiary), other than Dispositions permitted by clauses (a) through (h) of
Section 7.05.
"Assignment and Assumption" means an assignment and assumption
entered into by a Lender and an Eligible Assignee, with the consent of any party whose
consent is required by Section 10.06(b), and accepted by the Administrative Agent, in
substantially the form of Exhibit C.
"Attributable Indebtedness" means, on any date, (a) in respect of any finance
lease of any Person, the capitalized amount thereof that would appear on a balance sheet
of that Person prepared as of that date in accordance with GAAP, and (b) in respect of
any synthetic lease, the capitalized amount of the remaining lease payments that would
appear on a balance sheet if the lease were accounted for as a finance lease.
"Audited Financial Statements" means the audited consolidated balance
sheet of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025,
and the related consolidated statements of income, shareholders' equity, and cash flows
for that fiscal year, including the notes thereto, audited by Wainwright Lindqvist LLP.
6

"Available Amount" means, at any time, a cumulative amount equal to (a) the
greater of $25,000,000 and 20% of Consolidated EBITDA, plus (b) 50% of Consolidated
Net Income for the period from July 1, 2026 to the end of the most recent fiscal quarter
for which financial statements have been delivered (or, if negative, minus 100% of the
deficit), plus (c) the net cash proceeds of any issuance of Qualified Equity Interests,
minus (d) amounts previously applied to Restricted Payments and Investments in reliance
on the Available Amount.
"Availability Period" means, in respect of the Revolving Credit Facility, the
period from and including the Closing Date to the earliest of the Maturity Date, the date
of termination of the Revolving Credit Commitments under Section 2.07, and the date of
termination of the commitment of each Revolving Credit Lender to make Revolving
Credit Loans and of the obligation of the L/C Issuer to make L/C Credit Extensions under
Section 8.02.
"Bail-In Action" means the exercise of any Write-Down and Conversion
Powers by the applicable resolution authority in respect of any liability of an Affected
Financial Institution.
"Bail-In Legislation" means, with respect to any EEA Member Country
implementing Article 55 of Directive 2014/59/EU, the implementing law, regulation,
rule, or requirement for that country, and with respect to the United Kingdom, Part I of
the United Kingdom Banking Act 2009 and any other law applicable in the United
Kingdom relating to the resolution of unsound or failing banks, investment firms, or other
financial institutions or their affiliates.
"Bankruptcy Code" means Title 11 of the United States Code, as amended
from time to time.
"Base Rate" means for any day a fluctuating rate per annum equal to the highest
of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus one-half of one percent, (b) the rate of interest in effect
for that day as publicly announced from time to time by the Administrative Agent as its
"prime rate," (c) Term SOFR for a one-month tenor plus one percent, and (d) one percent;
any change in the Base Rate due to a change in any of these rates takes effect at the
opening of business on the day of the change.
"Benchmark Replacement" means, with respect to any Benchmark
Transition Event, the first alternative set forth below that can be determined by the
Administrative Agent: (a) Daily Simple SOFR; or (b) the sum of an alternate benchmark
7

rate selected by the Administrative Agent and the Borrower giving due consideration to
any selection or recommendation of a replacement rate by the Relevant Governmental
Body or any evolving or then-prevailing market convention for determining a rate of
interest as a replacement for the then-current Benchmark for syndicated credit facilities
denominated in Dollars, plus a related spread adjustment; provided that if the Benchmark
Replacement as so determined would be less than zero, it shall be deemed to be zero.
"Benchmark Transition Event" means a public statement or publication of
information by or on behalf of the administrator of the then-current Benchmark, the
regulatory supervisor for that administrator, or a Governmental Authority with
jurisdiction over it, announcing that the administrator has ceased or will cease to provide
all available tenors of that Benchmark permanently or indefinitely, or that all available
tenors are no longer, or as of a specified future date will no longer be, representative.
"Beneficial Ownership Certification" means a certification regarding
beneficial ownership or control as required by the Beneficial Ownership Regulation, in
form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and each
requesting Lender.
"Borrower Materials" has the meaning specified in Section 6.02, being
materials and information provided by or on behalf of the Borrower that are posted on the
Platform for the Lenders.
"Borrowing" means a Revolving Credit Borrowing, a Swing Line Borrowing, or
a Term A Borrowing, as the context may require, in each case consisting of simultaneous
Loans of the same Type and, in the case of Term SOFR Loans, having the same Interest
Period.
"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on
which commercial banks are authorized to close under the laws of, or are in fact closed
in, the state where the Administrative Agent's Office is located.
"Board of Directors" means, with respect to any Person, the board of directors
or comparable governing body of that Person, or any committee thereof duly authorized
to act on its behalf.
"Capital Expenditures" means, for any period, the aggregate of all
expenditures by the Borrower and its Subsidiaries for the acquisition or leasing of fixed
or capital assets or additions to equipment that would be required by GAAP to be
classified as capital expenditures, excluding expenditures financed with insurance or
8

condemnation proceeds or the proceeds of Asset Sales that are reinvested under Section
2.05(b)(ii).
"Cash Collateralize" means to pledge and deposit with the Administrative
Agent, for the benefit of the L/C Issuer or the Swing Line Lender and the Lenders, as
collateral for L/C Obligations or obligations of the Lenders to fund participations, cash or
deposit account balances in an amount equal to 103% of the Outstanding Amount of the
applicable obligations, under documentation satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.
"Cash Equivalents" means (a) securities issued or fully guaranteed by the
United States government having maturities of not more than twelve months; (b)
certificates of deposit and time deposits with maturities of not more than twelve months
issued by any Lender or any commercial bank having capital and surplus of not less than
$500,000,000; (c) commercial paper rated at least A-1 or P-1 maturing within 270 days;
and (d) money market funds substantially all of whose assets are investments of the kinds
described in clauses (a) through (c).
"Cash Management Bank" means any Person that, at the time it enters into a
Cash Management Agreement, is a Lender or an Affiliate of a Lender, or any Person that
is a party to a Cash Management Agreement with a Loan Party in existence on the
Closing Date and is a Lender or an Affiliate of a Lender on the Closing Date, in each case
in its capacity as a party to that Cash Management Agreement.
"CFC" means a Person that is a controlled foreign corporation within the
meaning of Section 957 of the Code, and "CFC Holdco" means a Domestic Subsidiary
substantially all of the assets of which consist of Equity Interests or indebtedness of one
or more CFCs.
"Cash Management Agreement" means any agreement to provide treasury
or cash management services, including deposit accounts, overdraft, credit or debit card,
purchasing card, electronic funds transfer, and automated clearing house services,
between any Loan Party and a Cash Management Bank.
"Change in Law" means the occurrence, after the date of this Agreement, of the
adoption or taking effect of any law, rule, regulation, or treaty, any change in its
administration, interpretation, or application by any Governmental Authority, or the
making or issuance of any request or directive by any Governmental Authority, whether
or not having the force of law.
9

"Change of Control" means an event or series of events by which (a) any
person or group becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of 35% or more of
the Equity Interests of the Borrower entitled to vote for members of its board of directors;
or (b) during any period of twelve consecutive months, a majority of the members of that
board cease to be composed of individuals who were members at the beginning of the
period or whose election was approved by a majority of those members; or (c) any
"change of control" or similar event occurs under any Indebtedness of the Borrower in
excess of the Threshold Amount.
"Closing Date" means June 12, 2026, the first date on which all the conditions
precedent in Section 4.01 were satisfied or waived in accordance with Section 10.01.
"Code" means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
"Collateral" means all of the property of the Loan Parties in which Liens are
purported to be granted under any of the Collateral Documents, which shall include
substantially all personal property of the Loan Parties and the Material Real Property, but
shall exclude Excluded Property.
"Collateral Documents" means, collectively, the Security Agreement, the
Mortgages, each intellectual property security agreement, each control agreement, and
each other agreement or instrument by which any Loan Party grants a Lien on its
property to the Administrative Agent for the benefit of the Secured Parties.
"Commitment" means a Term A Commitment or a Revolving Credit
Commitment, as the context may require.
"Committed Loan Notice" means a notice of a Term A Borrowing, a
Revolving Credit Borrowing, a conversion of Loans from one Type to the other, or a
continuation of Term SOFR Loans, which shall be substantially in the form of Exhibit A
or such other form as may be approved by the Administrative Agent, appropriately
completed and signed by a Responsible Officer of the Borrower.
"Compliance Certificate" means a certificate substantially in the form of
Exhibit B.
"Consolidated EBITDA" means, for any period, Consolidated Net Income for
that period plus, without duplication and to the extent deducted in calculating
Consolidated Net Income: (a) Consolidated Interest Charges; (b) the provision for
federal, state, local, and foreign income taxes; (c) depreciation and amortization expense;
10

(d) non-cash charges, including non-cash stock compensation and impairment of
goodwill; (e) restructuring charges, integration costs, and plant closure costs not
exceeding, together with clause (f), 15% of Consolidated EBITDA for the period; (f)
projected cost savings from actions taken within the period, reasonably identifiable and
expected to be realized within eighteen months; and (g) fees and expenses incurred in
connection with this Agreement and any Permitted Acquisition; minus non-cash gains
included in Consolidated Net Income.
"Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio" means, as of the end of any
fiscal quarter, the ratio of (a) Consolidated EBITDA minus unfinanced Capital
Expenditures and cash taxes paid, in each case for the four fiscal quarters then ended, to
(b) the sum of Consolidated Interest Charges paid in cash, scheduled principal payments
of Indebtedness, and Restricted Payments made in cash, in each case for that period.
"Consolidated Funded Indebtedness" means, as of any date, the sum
without duplication of all Indebtedness for borrowed money, the outstanding principal
amount of purchase money Indebtedness, Attributable Indebtedness, drawn and
unreimbursed amounts under letters of credit, and Guarantees of any of the foregoing, of
the Borrower and its Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis.
"Consolidated Interest Charges" means, for any period, the sum of all
interest, premium payments, debt discount, fees, charges, and related expenses in
connection with borrowed money or the deferred purchase price of assets, to the extent
treated as interest under GAAP, and the portion of rent expense under finance leases
treated as interest under GAAP, of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries on a consolidated
basis.
"Consolidated Net Income" means, for any period, the net income of the
Borrower and its Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, excluding extraordinary gains and
losses, the income of any Subsidiary to the extent its distributions are restricted, and the
income of any Person that is not a Subsidiary except to the extent of cash distributions
actually received.
"Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio" means, as of any date of
determination, the ratio of (a) Consolidated Funded Indebtedness as of that date, minus
unrestricted cash and Cash Equivalents of the Loan Parties not exceeding $40,000,000, to
(b) Consolidated EBITDA for the period of the four fiscal quarters most recently ended
for which financial statements have been delivered.
11

"Control" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or
cause the direction of the management or policies of a Person, whether through the ability
to exercise voting power, by contract, or otherwise; "Controlling" and "Controlled" have
meanings correlative thereto.
"Default Rate" means an interest rate equal to the interest rate otherwise
applicable to the relevant Loan plus two percent per annum, or, for amounts for which no
rate applies, the Base Rate plus the Applicable Rate for Base Rate Loans plus two percent
per annum.
"Defaulting Lender" means any Lender that has failed to fund any portion of
its Loans or participations within two Business Days of the date required, has notified the
Borrower or the Administrative Agent that it does not intend to comply with its funding
obligations, or has become the subject of a Bail-In Action or a proceeding under any
Debtor Relief Law.
"Disposition" means the sale, transfer, license, lease, or other disposition of any
property by any Person, including any sale, assignment, transfer, or other disposal of any
notes or accounts receivable, with or without recourse.
"Eligible Assignee" means any Person that meets the requirements to be an
assignee under Section 10.06(b), other than a natural person, a Defaulting Lender, or the
Borrower or any of its Affiliates.
"Environmental Laws" means all federal, state, local, and foreign statutes,
laws, regulations, ordinances, rules, judgments, orders, permits, and governmental
restrictions relating to pollution, the protection of the environment, or the release of any
materials into the environment.
"Event of Default" has the meaning specified in Section 8.01.
"Excluded Property" means (a) any fee-owned real property that is not
Material Real Property and all leasehold interests; (b) motor vehicles subject to
certificates of title; (c) Equity Interests in excess of 65% of the voting Equity Interests of
any Foreign Subsidiary; (d) any lease, license, or contract to the extent a grant of a Lien
would breach it; and (e) assets for which the cost of obtaining a security interest is
excessive in relation to the benefit to the Lenders, as reasonably determined by the
Administrative Agent.
12

"Existing Credit Agreement" means the Credit Agreement dated as of
September 30, 2021 among the Borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Wrenfield
Commercial Bank, as administrative agent, as amended prior to the Closing Date.
"Facility" means the Term A Facility or the Revolving Credit Facility, as the
context may require.
"Federal Funds Rate" means, for any day, the rate per annum calculated by
the Federal Reserve Bank of New York based on the day's federal funds transactions by
depository institutions, as published on the next succeeding Business Day as the federal
funds effective rate; if that rate is less than zero, it is deemed to be zero.
"Fee Letter" means the letter agreement dated May 8, 2026 among the
Borrower, the Administrative Agent, and Halden Bay Capital Markets LLC.
"Foreign Subsidiary" means any Subsidiary that is organized under the laws
of a jurisdiction other than the United States, a State thereof, or the District of Columbia.
"GAAP" means generally accepted accounting principles in the United States set
forth in the opinions and pronouncements of the Financial Accounting Standards Board,
consistently applied and as in effect from time to time, subject to Section 1.03.
"Guarantors" means, collectively, each Domestic Subsidiary of the Borrower
that is a party to the Guaranty on the Closing Date as listed in Schedule 5.13, and each
other Subsidiary that becomes a party to the Guaranty under Section 6.12.
"Incremental Facility" has the meaning specified in Section 2.16, being one or
more increases in the Revolving Credit Commitments or incremental term loans in an
aggregate amount not to exceed the greater of $100,000,000 and 100% of Consolidated
EBITDA, plus an additional amount so long as the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio,
on a Pro Forma Basis, does not exceed 3.00 to 1.00.
"Indebtedness" means, as to any Person at a particular time, without
duplication: all obligations for borrowed money and obligations evidenced by bonds,
debentures, notes, loan agreements, or similar instruments; the maximum amount
available to be drawn under letters of credit, bankers' acceptances, and similar
instruments; net obligations under any Swap Contract; obligations to pay the deferred
purchase price of property, other than trade accounts payable in the ordinary course not
more than 90 days past due; Attributable Indebtedness; obligations to purchase or redeem
Disqualified Equity Interests; and Guarantees of any of the foregoing.

ARTICLE II
THE COMMITMENTS AND CREDIT EXTENSIONS
2.01 Term A Loans. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, each Term A
Lender severally agrees to make a single loan to the Borrower on the Closing Date in an
amount not to exceed its Term A Commitment. The Term A Borrowing shall consist of
Term A Loans made simultaneously by the Term A Lenders in accordance with their
respective Applicable Percentages of the Term A Facility, which in the aggregate shall
equal $250,000,000. Amounts borrowed under this Section and repaid or prepaid may not
be reborrowed.
2.02 Revolving Credit Loans. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein,
each Revolving Credit Lender severally agrees to make loans to the Borrower from time
to time, on any Business Day during the Availability Period, in an aggregate amount not
to exceed at any time outstanding its Revolving Credit Commitment; provided that after
giving effect to any Revolving Credit Borrowing, the Total Revolving Credit
Outstandings shall not exceed $100,000,000. Within these limits the Borrower may
borrow, prepay, and reborrow.
2.03 Borrowings, Conversions, and Continuations. Each Borrowing, each
conversion of Loans from one Type to the other, and each continuation of Term SOFR
Loans shall be made upon the Borrower's irrevocable notice to the Administrative Agent,
which must be received by the Administrative Agent not later than 11:00 a.m. three
Business Days prior to the requested date of any Borrowing of, conversion to, or
18

Rate Loans. Each Borrowing of Term SOFR Loans shall be in a principal amount of
$2,000,000 or a whole multiple of $1,000,000 in excess thereof, and not more than eight
Interest Periods may be in effect at any time.
2.04 Letters of Credit. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, the L/C
Issuer agrees, in reliance upon the agreements of the Revolving Credit Lenders set forth
in this Section, to issue standby and commercial letters of credit for the account of the
Borrower or its Subsidiaries, and to amend or extend Letters of Credit previously issued
by it, provided that after giving effect to any such issuance the Outstanding Amount of
the L/C Obligations shall not exceed the Letter of Credit Sublimit. No Letter of Credit
shall have an expiry date later than the earlier of twelve months after its issuance and
seven days before the Maturity Date.
(a) Each Revolving Credit Lender irrevocably purchases from the L/C Issuer a
risk participation in each Letter of Credit in an amount equal to its Applicable
Percentage of the amount of that Letter of Credit.
(b) If any drawing is paid under a Letter of Credit, the Borrower shall reimburse
the L/C Issuer not later than 11:00 a.m. on the Business Day following notice of
the drawing, failing which the unreimbursed amount is deemed a request for a
Revolving Credit Borrowing of Base Rate Loans.
(c) The Borrower shall pay a Letter of Credit fee at the Applicable Rate on the
daily amount available to be drawn, quarterly in arrears, and a fronting fee of
0.125% per annum to the L/C Issuer for its own account.
2.05 Swing Line Loans. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, the
Swing Line Lender may in its sole discretion make loans to the Borrower from time to
time on any Business Day during the Availability Period in an aggregate amount not to
exceed at any time outstanding the Swing Line Sublimit. Each Swing Line Loan shall be

ARTICLE III
TAXES, YIELD PROTECTION, AND ILLEGALITY
3.01 Taxes. Any and all payments by or on account of any obligation of any Loan Party
shall be made without deduction or withholding for any Taxes, except as required by
applicable law. If any applicable law requires the deduction or withholding of any
Indemnified Taxes, the sum payable by the Loan Party shall be increased as necessary so
that after any required withholding the applicable Recipient receives an amount equal to
the sum it would have received had no such withholding been made. Each Lender shall
deliver to the Borrower and the Administrative Agent the applicable Internal Revenue
Service forms establishing any exemption from withholding.
3.02 Illegality. If any Lender determines that any law has made it unlawful for it to
make, maintain, or fund Loans whose interest is determined by reference to SOFR or
Term SOFR, then its obligation to make or continue Term SOFR Loans shall be
suspended until the circumstances giving rise to the determination no longer exist, and
the Borrower shall, if necessary to avoid the illegality, convert all such Loans of that
Lender to Base Rate Loans.
3.03 Inability to Determine Rates. If the Administrative Agent determines that Term
SOFR cannot be determined for any requested Interest Period, or the Required Lenders
determine that Term SOFR does not adequately reflect the cost to the Lenders of funding
the Loans, the obligation of the Lenders to make or continue Term SOFR Loans shall be
suspended, and any pending request shall be deemed a request for Base Rate Loans, until
a Benchmark Replacement is implemented in accordance with this Article.
3.04 Increased Costs. If any Change in Law shall impose any reserve, special deposit,
liquidity, or similar requirement against assets of any Lender, subject any Recipient to
23

any Taxes other than Indemnified Taxes and Excluded Taxes, or impose any other
condition affecting this Agreement, and the result is to increase the cost to the Lender of
making or maintaining any Loan or to reduce the amount received by it, the Borrower
will pay to the Lender such additional amounts as will compensate it for the additional
costs incurred or reduction suffered, upon delivery of a certificate setting forth the
amount in reasonable detail.
3.05 Compensation for Losses. Upon demand of any Lender, the Borrower shall
promptly compensate that Lender for any loss, cost, or expense incurred by it as a result
of any continuation, conversion, payment, or prepayment of any Term SOFR Loan on a
day other than the last day of its Interest Period, or any failure by the Borrower to
borrow, continue, or convert a Term SOFR Loan on the date specified in its notice,
excluding loss of anticipated profits.
3.06 Mitigation; Replacement of Lenders. If any Lender requests compensation
under Section 3.04, or the Borrower is required to pay additional amounts to a Lender
under Section 3.01, that Lender shall use reasonable efforts to designate a different
lending office if doing so would eliminate or reduce the amounts payable; if it does not,
the Borrower may replace that Lender with an Eligible Assignee in accordance with
Section 10.13.

5.13 free and clear of all Liens except those created under the Collateral Documents.

engaged principally in the business of purchasing or carrying margin stock, and no
proceeds of any Borrowing will be used for that purpose. Neither the Borrower nor any
Subsidiary is required to be registered as an "investment company" under the Investment
Company Act of 1940.

after giving effect to the transactions contemplated by the Loan Documents to occur on
the Closing Date.
5.13 Sanctions; Anti-Corruption. Neither the Borrower nor any Subsidiary, nor to
the knowledge of the Borrower any director, officer, or employee thereof, is an individual
or entity that is the subject of any Sanctions or located in a Designated Jurisdiction. The
Borrower and its Subsidiaries have conducted their businesses in compliance in all
material respects with applicable anti-corruption laws and have instituted policies
designed to promote compliance with them.
ARTICLE VI
AFFIRMATIVE COVENANTS
6.01 Financial Statements. The Borrower shall deliver to the Administrative Agent
for distribution to each Lender (a) as soon as available, and in any event within 90 days
27

after the end of each fiscal year, a consolidated balance sheet of the Borrower and its
Subsidiaries as at the end of that fiscal year and the related consolidated statements of
income, changes in shareholders' equity, and cash flows, audited and accompanied by a
report and opinion of an independent certified public accountant of nationally recognized
standing not subject to any "going concern" qualification; and (b) within 45 days after the
end of each of the first three fiscal quarters, the corresponding unaudited consolidated
statements, certified by a Responsible Officer.
6.02 Certificates; Other Information. Concurrently with the delivery of the financial
statements under Section 6.01, the Borrower shall deliver a duly completed Compliance
Certificate signed by its chief financial officer, and, within 60 days after the beginning of
each fiscal year, an annual budget of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries on a consolidated
basis, including forecasts of balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements
for that fiscal year on a quarterly basis.
6.03 Notices. The Borrower shall promptly notify the Administrative Agent of the
occurrence of any Default; of any matter that has resulted or could reasonably be
expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; of the occurrence of any ERISA Event;
of any material change in accounting policies or financial reporting practices; and of any
announcement by a rating agency of any change in a debt rating of the Borrower.
6.04 Payment of Obligations. The Borrower shall, and shall cause each Subsidiary
to, pay and discharge as the same become due and payable all tax liabilities, assessments,
and governmental charges upon it or its properties, and all lawful claims that, if unpaid,
would by law become a Lien upon its property, unless contested in good faith by
appropriate proceedings with adequate reserves.
6.05 Preservation of Existence. The Borrower shall, and shall cause each Subsidiary
to, preserve, renew, and maintain in full force and effect its legal existence and good
standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its organization, except in a transaction
permitted by Section 7.04 or 7.05, and take all reasonable action to maintain all rights,
privileges, permits, licenses, and franchises necessary or desirable in the normal conduct
of its business.
6.06 Maintenance of Properties and Insurance. The Borrower shall maintain all
of its material properties and equipment necessary in the operation of its business in good
working order and condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted, and shall maintain
insurance in accordance with Section 5.10, naming the Administrative Agent as
additional insured and lender loss payee, with thirty days' notice of cancellation.
28

6.07 Books and Records; Inspection Rights. The Borrower shall maintain proper
books of record and account and shall permit representatives of the Administrative Agent
to visit and inspect its properties, examine its corporate, financial, and operating records,
and discuss its affairs with its directors, officers, and independent accountants, not more
than once per fiscal year at the Borrower's expense while no Event of Default exists.
6.08 Compliance with Laws. The Borrower shall comply in all respects with the
requirements of all laws and all orders, writs, injunctions, and decrees applicable to it or
to its business or property, except where the requirement is being contested in good faith
or where failure to comply could not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse
Effect, and shall maintain in effect policies designed to promote compliance by the
Borrower, its Subsidiaries, and their directors, officers, and employees with
Anti-Corruption Laws and Sanctions.
6.09 Environmental Matters. The Borrower shall, and shall cause each Subsidiary to,
comply in all material respects with all Environmental Laws, obtain and renew all
environmental permits necessary for its operations, and conduct any investigation, study,
sampling, testing, remedial, or other corrective action required under Environmental
Laws, including completion of the remediation at the Linden Cross plant in accordance
with the consent order and the schedule approved by the state environmental agency.
6.10 Use of Proceeds. The Borrower shall use the proceeds of the Credit Extensions
to refinance the Existing Credit Agreement on the Closing Date, to pay fees and expenses
in connection with this Agreement, and for working capital, Capital Expenditures,
Permitted Acquisitions, Restricted Payments permitted hereunder, and other general
corporate purposes not in contravention of any law or any Loan Document.
6.11 Post-Closing Obligations. The Borrower shall deliver, or cause to be delivered,
to the Administrative Agent the following, each in form and substance reasonably
satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, within the time periods specified (or such later
dates as the Administrative Agent may agree in its sole discretion): (a) within 30 days
after the Closing Date, deposit account control agreements for each deposit account of a
Loan Party other than Excluded Accounts; (b) within 60 days after the Closing Date,
insurance endorsements naming the Administrative Agent as additional insured and
lender loss payee; and (c) within 90 days after the Closing Date, a Mortgage, title
insurance policy, survey, flood determination, and local counsel opinion for each
Material Real Property.
29

6.12 Additional Guarantors and Collateral. Within 45 days after any Person
becomes a Domestic Subsidiary (other than an Excluded Subsidiary), or any Domestic
Subsidiary ceases to be an Excluded Subsidiary, the Borrower shall cause that Person to
become a Guarantor by executing a joinder to the Guaranty and the Security Agreement
and to deliver the documents, opinions, and filings the Administrative Agent reasonably
requests to perfect the Liens on its property.
ARTICLE VII
NEGATIVE COVENANTS
7.01 Liens. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any Subsidiary to, create, incur,
assume, or suffer to exist any Lien upon any of its property, whether now owned or
hereafter acquired, other than the following:
(a) Liens pursuant to any Loan Document;
(b) Liens existing on the Closing Date and listed on Schedule 7.01 and any
renewals or extensions thereof, provided the property covered is not changed and
the amount secured is not increased;
(c) Liens for taxes not yet due or being contested in good faith, and carriers',
warehousemen's, mechanics', and similar Liens arising in the ordinary course for
amounts not overdue for more than 30 days;
(d) Liens securing purchase money Indebtedness and Attributable Indebtedness
permitted by Section 7.02(e), provided they do not extend to any property other
than the property acquired with that Indebtedness;
(e) Liens on property of Foreign Subsidiaries securing Indebtedness of Foreign
Subsidiaries permitted by Section 7.02(g); and
(f) other Liens securing obligations in an aggregate amount not to exceed the
greater of $20,000,000 and 15% of Consolidated EBITDA at any time
outstanding.
7.02 Indebtedness. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any Subsidiary to,
create, incur, assume, or suffer to exist any Indebtedness, except: (a) Indebtedness under
the Loan Documents; (b) Indebtedness outstanding on the Closing Date and listed on
Schedule 7.02 and refinancings thereof not increasing the principal amount; (c)
intercompany Indebtedness permitted as an Investment; (d) obligations under Swap
Contracts entered into to hedge actual exposures and not for speculation; (e) purchase
30

money Indebtedness and Attributable Indebtedness not exceeding the greater of
$35,000,000 and 25% of Consolidated EBITDA; (f) unsecured Indebtedness so long as
the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio on a Pro Forma Basis does not exceed 3.25 to
1.00 and it matures at least 91 days after the Maturity Date; and (g) Indebtedness of
Foreign Subsidiaries not exceeding $25,000,000 at any time outstanding.
7.03 Investments. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any Subsidiary to, make
any Investments, except Investments held in the form of Cash Equivalents; advances to
officers, directors, and employees not exceeding $1,500,000 at any time outstanding;
Investments by Loan Parties in other Loan Parties; Investments by Loan Parties in
Subsidiaries that are not Loan Parties not exceeding the greater of $30,000,000 and 20%
of Consolidated EBITDA; Permitted Acquisitions; Investments in the Basalt Drive Inks
joint venture not exceeding $8,000,000 in any fiscal year; and other Investments not
exceeding the Available Amount.
7.04 Fundamental Changes. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any
Subsidiary to, merge, dissolve, liquidate, consolidate with or into another Person, or
Dispose of all or substantially all of its assets, except that any Subsidiary may merge with
the Borrower (if the Borrower is the continuing Person) or with any other Subsidiary (if a
Loan Party is the continuing Person when a Loan Party is involved), and any Subsidiary
may Dispose of all or substantially all its assets to the Borrower or another Loan Party.
7.05 Dispositions. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any Subsidiary to, make
any Disposition except Dispositions of obsolete or worn-out property, inventory in the
ordinary course, equipment exchanged for similar replacement property, property to a
Loan Party, licenses of intellectual property in the ordinary course, and other Dispositions
for fair market value, at least 75% in cash, so long as the aggregate book value of all
property so Disposed of in any fiscal year does not exceed 10% of consolidated total
assets.
7.06 Restricted Payments. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any Subsidiary
to, declare or make any Restricted Payment, except that each Subsidiary may make
Restricted Payments to the Borrower and to other Loan Parties; the Borrower may
declare and make dividends payable solely in its common stock; the Borrower may
repurchase stock from former employees in an amount not to exceed $5,000,000 in any
fiscal year; and the Borrower may make other Restricted Payments so long as no Event of
Default exists and the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio on a Pro Forma Basis does not
exceed 2.75 to 1.00, or in an amount not exceeding the Available Amount.
31

7.07 Change in Nature of Business. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any
Subsidiary to, engage in any material line of business substantially different from those
lines of business conducted by the Borrower and its Subsidiaries on the Closing Date -
the manufacture and sale of corrugated, folding carton, flexible, molded fiber, and label
packaging and related printing, inks, and services - or any business substantially related,
complementary, or incidental thereto.
7.08 Transactions with Affiliates. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any
Subsidiary to, enter into any transaction of any kind with any Affiliate of the Borrower,
whether or not in the ordinary course of business, other than on fair and reasonable terms
substantially as favorable to the Borrower or the Subsidiary as would be obtainable in a
comparable arm's length transaction with a Person other than an Affiliate, except
transactions among Loan Parties and Restricted Payments permitted by Section 7.06.
7.09 Burdensome Agreements. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit any
Subsidiary to, enter into any Contractual Obligation that limits the ability of any
Subsidiary to make Restricted Payments to the Borrower or any Guarantor, of any
Subsidiary to Guarantee the Obligations, or of the Borrower or any Subsidiary to create
Liens on its property in favor of the Administrative Agent, other than customary
restrictions in joint venture agreements and in agreements governing purchase money
Indebtedness.
7.10 Use of Proceeds. The Borrower shall not use the proceeds of any Credit
Extension, whether directly or indirectly, to purchase or carry margin stock, or to fund
any activity or business of or with any Person that is the subject of Sanctions or in any
Designated Jurisdiction, or in violation of any anti-corruption law.
7.11 Sale and Leaseback Transactions. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it permit
any Subsidiary to, enter into any arrangement whereby it sells or transfers any property,
real or personal, used or useful in its business, and thereafter rents or leases that property
or other property that it intends to use for substantially the same purpose, except
sale-leaseback transactions involving property with an aggregate fair market value not
exceeding $25,000,000 over the term of this Agreement, the Attributable Indebtedness of
which is permitted under Section 7.02(e).
7.12 Prepayments of Other Indebtedness. The Borrower shall not, nor shall it
permit any Subsidiary to, prepay, redeem, purchase, defease, or otherwise satisfy prior to
scheduled maturity any unsecured or subordinated Indebtedness, except refinancings
permitted by Section 7.02, prepayments made with the net cash proceeds of Qualified
32

Equity Interests, and other prepayments not exceeding the Available Amount so long as
no Event of Default exists and the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio on a Pro Forma
Basis does not exceed 3.00 to 1.00.
7.13 Amendments of Organization Documents; Fiscal Year. The Borrower
shall not amend any of its Organization Documents in a manner materially adverse to the
Lenders, and shall not change its fiscal year, which ends on December 31, without the
consent of the Administrative Agent, provided that the Borrower may change its fiscal
year upon notice, in which case the Borrower and the Administrative Agent will make
any adjustments to this Agreement necessary to reflect the change.
7.14 Financial Covenants. The Borrower shall not permit:
(a) the Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio as of the end of any fiscal quarter,
commencing with the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026, to be greater than
3.75 to 1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending on or before June 30, 2027, and 3.50 to
1.00 thereafter; provided that the Borrower may elect, by notice with the
Compliance Certificate for the quarter in which a Permitted Acquisition with
consideration of $75,000,000 or more is consummated, to increase the maximum
ratio by 0.50 for that quarter and the three following quarters, not more than twice
during the term of this Agreement; or
(b) the Consolidated Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio as of the end of any fiscal
quarter to be less than 1.25 to 1.00.
ARTICLE VIII
EVENTS OF DEFAULT AND REMEDIES
8.01 Events of Default. Any of the following shall constitute an Event of Default:
(a) the Borrower fails to pay when due any amount of principal of any Loan or
L/C Obligation, or within three Business Days after the same becomes due, any
interest, fee, or other amount payable hereunder;
(b) the Borrower fails to perform or observe any term, covenant, or agreement
contained in Section 6.03(a), 6.05(a), or 6.11 or Article VII;
(c) any Loan Party fails to perform or observe any other covenant contained in
any Loan Document and the failure continues for 30 days after notice from the
Administrative Agent;
33

(d) any representation or warranty made by any Loan Party proves to have been
incorrect or misleading in any material respect when made;
(e) the Borrower or any Subsidiary fails to make any payment when due in respect
of any Indebtedness having an aggregate principal amount of more than the
Threshold Amount, or any event occurs the effect of which is to cause or permit
that Indebtedness to become due before its stated maturity;
(f) the Borrower or any Subsidiary institutes or consents to the institution of any
proceeding under any Debtor Relief Law, or makes a general assignment for the
benefit of creditors, or any such proceeding instituted against it continues
undismissed for 60 calendar days;
(g) one or more final judgments for the payment of money in an aggregate amount
exceeding the Threshold Amount (to the extent not covered by insurance as to
which the insurer has not disputed coverage) is entered against the Borrower or
any Subsidiary and is not discharged or stayed for 30 consecutive days;
(h) an ERISA Event occurs which has resulted or could reasonably be expected to
result in liability of the Borrower in an aggregate amount in excess of the
Threshold Amount;
(i) any Loan Document ceases to be in full force and effect, or any Lien purported
to be created by any Collateral Document ceases to be a valid and perfected Lien
on Collateral with a fair market value in excess of $10,000,000; or
(j) there occurs any Change of Control.
8.02 Remedies upon Event of Default. If any Event of Default occurs and is
continuing, the Administrative Agent shall, at the request of, or may, with the consent of,
the Required Lenders, declare the commitment of each Lender to make Loans and any
obligation of the L/C Issuer to make L/C Credit Extensions to be terminated; declare the
unpaid principal amount of all outstanding Loans, all interest accrued and unpaid thereon,
and all other amounts owing hereunder to be immediately due and payable, without
presentment, demand, protest, or other notice of any kind; require that the Borrower Cash
Collateralize the L/C Obligations; and exercise all rights and remedies available to it and
the Lenders under the Loan Documents or applicable law. Upon an Event of Default
under Section 8.01(f), these consequences occur automatically.
34

8.03 Application of Funds. After the exercise of remedies, any amounts received on
account of the Obligations shall be applied: first, to fees, indemnities, expenses, and other
amounts payable to the Administrative Agent; second, to fees and other amounts payable
to the Lenders and the L/C Issuer; third, to accrued and unpaid interest and fees ratably;
fourth, to principal of the Loans, L/C Borrowings, and obligations under Secured Hedge
Agreements and Secured Cash Management Agreements, and to Cash Collateralize
undrawn Letters of Credit, ratably; and last, the balance, if any, to the Borrower or as
otherwise required by law.

Administrative Agent to take such actions on its behalf and to exercise such powers as

for the benefit of the Administrative Agent, the Lenders, and the L/C Issuer, and neither

them.

the same rights and powers in its capacity as a Lender as any other Lender and may
exercise them as though it were not the Administrative Agent, and it and its Affiliates
may accept deposits from, lend money to, act as financial adviser to, and generally
engage in any kind of business with the Borrower or any Subsidiary as if it were not the

obligations except those expressly set forth herein and in the other Loan Documents, and

be liable for any action taken or not taken by it with the consent of the Required Lenders

court of competent jurisdiction by final and nonappealable judgment.

time give notice of its resignation to the Lenders, the L/C Issuer, and the Borrower. Upon

receipt of any such notice, the Required Lenders shall have the right, with the consent of
the Borrower while no Event of Default exists, to appoint a successor, which shall be a
bank with an office in the United States having combined capital and surplus of at least

Administrative Agent to release any Lien on property granted to or held by it under any

ceases to be a Subsidiary as a result of a transaction permitted hereunder.

Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative - Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2026
At a Glance
Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative is a farmer-owned supply and marketing cooperative serving 6,882 active
members across ten counties from twelve locations in eleven states. Members own the cooperative, elect its
board, and share in its earnings through patronage refunds based on the business they do with it.

Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative - Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2026
To Our Members
Fiscal 2026 tested every part of the cooperative. Revenue rose 7.4% to $2,832,126 thousand, while gross
margin grew to $248,105 thousand. Grain prices spent most of the year below the cost of production for many
of you, fertilizer prices eased only in the spring, and drought in the southern counties cut sorghum yields by as
much as a third. Through it all, your cooperative kept its elevators open longer during harvest, extended input
financing to 412 members, and delivered fuel and propane through the coldest January in eleven years.
Local savings before income taxes were $81,416 thousand, of which $71,646 thousand is patronage-sourced
and will be allocated to members. The board has voted to pay 40% of the allocation in cash in December, the
highest cash percentage since fiscal 2014, and to retire the remaining 2011 and 2012 allocated equity of
members who have reached age 70 or whose estates have asked for it.
We invested in the places that will matter for the next twenty years: a 1.2 million bushel concrete bin at
Tamsin Valley, a pellet mill rebuild at Silverlode, and the brine system at the Kestrel Ridge dairy plant. Our
employees worked 1.9 million hours with a recordable injury rate of 1.6, the best in the cooperative's history,
and we thank them for it.
Next year we will finish the shuttle loader expansion at Oriel Junction, bring precision agronomy services to
every agronomy location, and begin a review of our energy business, where the shift to renewable diesel is
changing what members need from us. We will continue to report to you plainly about what we do and how it
turns out.
Respectfully, Corinne Baptiste, Chair of the Board, and Ilse Chakrabarti, President and Chief
Executive Officer

Strategic Plan 2024-2028: Progress

year.

The two goals behind schedule share a cause: weaker earnings in fiscal 2024 slowed equity retirement, and a

updates the plan in fiscal 2027. Capital spent under the plan so far totals $63,990 thousand of the $109,128

Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative - Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2026
Risk Factors
The following risks could materially affect the cooperative's results, financial condition, or ability to return
equity to members. They are not the only risks we face.
Commodity prices. Most of our revenue comes from buying and selling grain, fertilizer, fuel, feed
ingredients, and milk, whose prices move with world markets. We hedge grain and some energy positions with
exchange-traded futures, but basis, spreads, and the timing of member pricing decisions remain exposed, and a
sharp move can turn a profitable position into a loss within days.
Weather and crop size. Drought, hail, flooding, and early frost change how much grain members harvest
and how much fertilizer and crop protection they buy. A short crop in our trade area reduces grain handling
and drying income, and a wet spring can compress the application season into a few weeks and leave product
unsold.
Member concentration. Our 200 largest members account for about 46% of gross margin. If several of
them retire, sell their operations, or move business to a competitor, our volumes and margins would fall more
than the number of members lost would suggest.
Competition from investor-owned companies. Regional and national grain companies, input retailers,
and fuel distributors compete for every bushel and every gallon in our trade area. Several have greater financial
resources and can sustain lower margins for longer than we can.
Counterparty and credit risk. We extend seasonal credit to members for inputs and hold deferred-price
contracts on their behalf. A widespread farm income downturn would raise bad debts. We also depend on
futures commission merchants and grain buyers to perform their contracts.
Liquidity during seasonal peaks. Our borrowing needs peak in the fall, when grain and fertilizer
inventories and margin calls are highest. If our lender reduced the seasonal facility or margin calls exceeded
our available credit, we might have to sell inventory or close positions at unfavorable prices.
Interest rates. Higher interest rates raise the cost of carrying inventory and of our term debt, and they reduce
the carry that makes grain storage profitable.
Dependence on rail service. Our shuttle loaders depend on two railroads for car supply. Service
disruptions during harvest can fill our storage and force us to stop receiving grain or to pay members less for it.
Hazardous materials. We store and transport anhydrous ammonia, propane, and fuels. A release or
explosion could injure employees or neighbors, damage property, lead to fines, and harm the cooperative's
reputation.
Grain dust and confined spaces. Grain elevators present risks of dust explosions and engulfment.
Despite our training and permit-required entry procedures, a serious accident could cause loss of life and long
shutdowns.
Food safety in dairy processing. Contamination of milk or cheese could require a recall, harm
consumers, and damage our relationships with the retailers and food companies that buy our products.
Environmental regulation. Changes in rules on nutrient runoff, air emissions from dryers and feed mills,
and wastewater from the dairy plant could require capital spending that does not increase revenue.
32

Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative - Annual Report, Fiscal Year 2026
Renewable fuels policy. Changes in federal and state renewable fuel standards and tax credits affect the
value of the corn and soybean oil we market and the economics of renewable diesel we sell.
Trade policy. Tariffs and export restrictions imposed by the United States or its trading partners can reduce
export demand for grain and lower local prices, as happened in fiscal 2019.
Labor availability. We compete for drivers holding commercial licenses with hazardous materials
endorsements, certified applicators, and plant mechanics. Shortages raise wages and can delay deliveries at the
busiest times of year.
Aging facilities. Several of our elevators and the oldest feed mill were built before 1970. Maintaining them
requires steady capital spending, and an unexpected structural failure could close a location during harvest.
Information technology and cybersecurity. We rely on our grain accounting, dispatch, and payment
systems to serve members. A ransomware attack or system failure during harvest could stop scales and
settlements for days.
Joint venture performance. Our share of earnings from the Bellmoor cheese joint venture depends on
decisions we do not control alone and on cheese markets that have been volatile.
Pension obligations. The frozen defined benefit pension plan remains underfunded. Lower discount rates
or poor investment returns would increase required contributions.
Equity retirement expectations. Members expect allocated equity to be retired on a regular cycle. If
earnings fall, the board may slow retirements, which could weaken member loyalty.
Tax treatment of patronage. The cooperative's income tax position depends on its qualifying as a
cooperative under federal tax law. A change in that treatment would reduce the amount available for patronage
refunds.
Climate change. Longer droughts and more intense storms could change what crops our members grow and
where, reduce yields over time, and increase the cost of insurance for our facilities.
Consolidation of farms. Fewer, larger farms buy more directly from manufacturers and market grain to end
users, bypassing local cooperatives. This trend could reduce our share of the business in our trade area.
Governance and succession. The cooperative depends on a small group of senior managers and on
directors who are working farmers. The loss of key people without a successor could disrupt operations.

Revenue for fiscal 2026 was $2,832,126 thousand compared with $2,635,994 thousand in fiscal 2025. Changes
in commodity prices explain most of the movement in revenue from year to year; gross margin, which is
revenue less the cost of goods sold, is the better measure of how much business members did with the
cooperative and how profitably it was handled.
Gross margin was $248,105 thousand. Operating expenses were $166,689 thousand, or 67.2% of gross margin.
Wages and benefits rose 5.8% with a 4% general increase and higher health plan costs; repairs rose with the
age of our elevators; and insurance premiums rose 11% after a hard market renewal.
Liquidity: the cooperative ended the year with working capital of $84,280 thousand and $62,947 thousand
available under its seasonal revolving credit facility with Kingsfold Farm Credit Bank. Seasonal borrowings
peaked in November at $87,226 thousand, when grain and fertilizer inventories are highest. The cooperative
was in compliance with all loan covenants at year end.
Capital resources: the board approved a capital budget of $24.6 million for fiscal 2027, to be funded from
operating cash flow and a term loan advance for the Oriel Junction shuttle loader. Equity retirement is planned
at $4.0 million.
Critical accounting estimates: inventories of grain and grain-related contracts are carried at net realizable
value; the allowance for doubtful accounts reflects specific reserves on 23 accounts and a general reserve
based on aging; pension obligations depend on a discount rate that rose to 5.4% from 5.1%.

Note 1 - Nature of Operations
Tamsin Valley Farmers Cooperative is an agricultural cooperative organized under the laws of New Mexico. It
markets grain and milk for its members and supplies them with fertilizer, crop protection products, fuel,
propane, feed, and farm and ranch merchandise from twelve locations. The consolidated financial statements
include the accounts of the Cooperative and its wholly owned subsidiaries; its 50% interest in the Bellmoor
cheese joint venture is accounted for using the equity method.
Note 2 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
Grain inventories, forward purchase and sale contracts, and exchange-traded futures and options are valued at
net realizable value, with changes recognized in cost of goods sold. Other inventories are valued at the lower
of cost (first-in, first-out) and net realizable value. Revenue is recognized when control of goods passes to the
customer, generally on delivery or when the member prices grain. Patronage refunds received from other
cooperatives are recorded when notification is received.
Property, plant and equipment is depreciated on the straight-line method over estimated useful lives of 10 to 40
years for buildings and 3 to 15 years for equipment.

seasonal program at a rate of prime plus 1.25%, due December 1.

# Separation Agreement and General Release

This Separation Agreement and General Release (this "Agreement") is entered into as of April 6, 2026 by and between Mossgiel Biomedical Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), and Corinne Abernathy ("Employee").

## Recitals

A. Employee has been employed by the Company since June 2, 2019, most recently as Director of Clinical Operations, under an Employment Agreement dated June 2, 2019 (the "Employment Agreement").

B. Employee's employment with the Company ended on March 31, 2026 (the "Separation Date") as part of the consolidation of the Company's clinical operations function in its Wrenfield, Ohio facility.

C. The Company and Employee wish to resolve fully and finally all matters between them, including any arising out of Employee's employment and its termination.

# 1. Final Pay and Benefits

The Company has paid Employee all base salary earned through the Separation Date and all accrued but unused paid time off (96.5 hours), whether or not Employee signs this Agreement. Employee's group health coverage continued through the end of the month that includes the Separation Date.

# 2. Severance Benefits

Provided that Employee signs this Agreement within the consideration period in Section 6 and does not revoke it, the Company will provide the following (the "Severance Benefits"), which Employee acknowledges exceed anything to which Employee is otherwise entitled:

| **Benefit** | **Amount** | **Timing** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base salary continuation | $48,750.00 | Thirteen equal biweekly installments on regular payroll dates, beginning on the first payroll date after the Effective Date |
| COBRA premium reimbursement | Up to $11,340.00 | Monthly, for coverage through September 30, 2026 or earlier eligibility for other coverage |
| Prorated 2026 bonus | $9,200.00 | Lump sum within thirty days after the Effective Date |
| Outplacement services | $4,500.00 | Paid directly to the provider; must begin within ninety days |

# 3. Equity Awards

The 4,200 vested stock options held by Employee on the Separation Date will remain exercisable until December 31, 2026, notwithstanding the shorter post-termination exercise period in the applicable award agreements. All unvested options and restricted stock units were forfeited on the Separation Date.

# 4. General Release of Claims

In exchange for the Severance Benefits, Employee, on behalf of Employee and Employee's heirs and assigns, releases the Company, its affiliates, and their officers, directors, employees, and agents from all claims, known or unknown, arising on or before the date Employee signs this Agreement, including claims arising out of Employee's employment or its termination, claims under the Employment Agreement, and claims under federal, state, and local laws prohibiting discrimination, harassment, or retaliation, including the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. This release does not waive rights that cannot be waived by law, rights to vested benefits, or the right to file a charge with a government agency, although Employee waives any right to recover money in connection with such a charge.

# 5. Return of Property; Continuing Obligations

Employee confirms that Employee has returned all Company property, including the Company laptop and badge, and has not retained copies of Company documents. Employee's obligations under the Employee Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement remain in effect. Each party agrees not to make statements that disparage the other; the Company's obligation is limited to instructing the members of its executive leadership team.

# 6. Consideration and Revocation

Employee has twenty-one days to consider this Agreement and must sign and return it no later than April 27, 2026. Employee is advised to consult an attorney before signing. Employee may revoke this Agreement within seven days after signing it by written notice to the Company's Chief People Officer. This Agreement becomes effective and enforceable on the eighth day after Employee signs it without revoking it (the "Effective Date").

# 7. Cooperation

For six months after the Separation Date, Employee will reasonably cooperate with the Company in transitioning Employee's responsibilities and in any regulatory inspection or litigation concerning matters within Employee's knowledge. The Company will reimburse reasonable expenses and pay $150 per hour for time spent at its request after the first ten hours.

# 8. Miscellaneous

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Ohio. It is the entire agreement between the parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior agreements, except the agreements expressly preserved in Sections 3 and 5. It may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties, and may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Nothing in this Agreement is an admission of wrongdoing by either party.

This First Amendment to Distribution Agreement (this "Amendment") is made and entered into as of
July 15, 2026 by and between Hollowell Kitchenware Inc., an Ohio corporation ("Supplier"), and
Driftmoor Home Goods Distributors LLC, a Washington limited liability company ("Distributor").
Recitals
A. Supplier and Distributor are parties to a Distribution Agreement dated January 4, 2024 (the
"Agreement"), under which Distributor is Supplier's exclusive distributor of cookware, bakeware, and
kitchen tools to independent retailers in Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming.
B. Distributor has opened a warehouse in Halden Bay, Washington, and the parties wish to expand the
territory, revise the price schedule and minimum purchase commitments, and extend the term.
The parties therefore agree as follows:
1. Territory. Schedule A of the Agreement is amended to add the States of Oregon and Washington to
the Territory. Distributor's exclusivity in the added States is limited to independent retailers with fewer
than ten stores; Supplier may continue to sell directly to the national chains listed in Schedule A-1.
2. Prices. The price schedule attached to this Amendment as Schedule B replaces Schedule B of the
Agreement for all orders placed on or after September 1, 2026. Orders placed before that date are
invoiced at the prices in effect when placed. Supplier may adjust prices once in each calendar year on
ninety days' notice, by no more than the percentage change in its published wholesale price list.
3. Minimum Purchases. Section 5.2 of the Agreement is amended so that Distributor's minimum
annual purchases, measured at net invoice prices, are $1,850,000 for 2026, $2,400,000 for 2027,
$2,750,000 for 2028, and $3,100,000 for 2029. If Distributor fails to meet the minimum for a year,
Supplier's only remedy is to end Distributor's exclusivity in the added States on sixty days' notice.
4. Term. Section 12.1 of the Agreement is amended to extend the term through December 31, 2029.
Either party may terminate the Agreement without cause on one hundred eighty days' notice given after
December 31, 2027.
5. Marketing Support. Supplier will provide Distributor a cooperative marketing allowance of two
percent of net purchases in the added States during the first eighteen months after the date of this
Amendment, to be used for trade shows, retailer training, and in-store displays approved in advance by
Supplier.
6. Effect of Amendment. Except as amended by this Amendment, the Agreement remains in full force
and effect. If this Amendment conflicts with the Agreement, this Amendment controls. This Amendment
may be signed in counterparts, and a scanned signature is as effective as an original.
